lines.text: Living alone: about 20% of all Dutch people live alone — ten times as many as in 1950, and the group keeps growing.
Reasons: people are single, divorced [gescheiden], or their partner has died; young people [jongeren] often go live alone first.
Some people do have a relationship but want to live alone: a LAT relationship — living apart together [latrelatie].
Living with a partner: two people can be married — a marriage [huwelijk], regulated in the law [wet].
Slightly less than half of Dutch people are married.
More and more people live together without marriage, with:
a registered partnership [geregistreerd partnerschap]: almost the same rights and duties [rechten en plichten] as a married couple [stel], also regulated in the law;
a cohabitation contract [samenlevingscontract]: they arrange their rights and duties themselves;
living together without arrangements — if they split up, this can cause problems.
On an official [officieel] form you often fill in your marital status [burgerlijke staat]: married [gehuwd], registered partnership, divorced or unmarried [ongehuwd].
Living in a family: on average 1.5 children [gemiddeld 1,5 kind] are born per woman in the Netherlands, and this number is still decreasing.
Most children live with their own two parents.
There are more and more families with only one parent [één ouder].
When children of different fathers and mothers live in one family, this is called a blended family [samengesteld gezin]; the children get a stepfather [stiefvader] or stepmother [stiefmoeder].
Homosexuality: a man can also be attracted to men [op mannen vallen], a woman to women.
Lhbtiq+ means: lesbisch, homoseksueel, biseksueel, transgender, interseksueel, queer, plus everything not mentioned.
According to a study from 2024, 18% of Dutch people are not heterosexual [heteroseksueel].
You cannot change homosexuality: it is already fixed [staat al vast] before you are born, just like the color of your eyes.
In the Netherlands homosexual and heterosexual people have the same rights [dezelfde rechten] under the law; all kinds of discrimination [discriminatie] are forbidden [verboden].
The same-sex marriage [homohuwelijk] has been possible in the Netherlands since 2001 — the Netherlands was the first country where two men or two women could marry.
They can also have children together.
The symbol is the rainbow flag [regenboogvlag].
